solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Notices Greek character being included in 'second-rate writers'

indicators.note: the Greek letter is set inside the word for notices, so being included signals a container

parts.note: posters are notices put up on walls
eta is the seventh letter of the Greek alphabet

explanation.surface: A complaint that a Greek letter has been slipped into a piece about poor writers.
explanation.definitionFit: A poetaster is a writer of trivial or inferior verse, a synonym for a second-rate writer.

clue.text: Bullet needs little time — fast mover

parts.note: T is the standard abbreviation for time
a racer is something built to move fast

explanation.surface: A bullet's requirements: a moment and a speedster.
explanation.definitionFit: A tracer is a bullet that leaves a visible trail so its path can be followed.

clue.text: Blonde he gets into trouble — is under a moral obligation

indicators.note: getting into trouble suggests the letters of these words end up in disarray

explanation.surface: A fair-haired man runs into difficulty and feels he owes someone.
explanation.definitionFit: Being beholden means owing a debt of gratitude, a moral obligation to someone.

clue.text: Part of mountain that sounds huge

indicators.note: the clue says the word sounds like huge, so a word spoken the same way is wanted

parts.note: massive means huge

explanation.surface: A mountain feature whose name suggests enormity.
explanation.definitionFit: A massif is a compact group of mountains forming part of a larger range.

clue.text: View offered by soldiers in republic

indicators.note: the soldiers are placed inside the name of the republic

parts.note: Panama is a republic in Central America
OR, other ranks, is the usual abbreviation for ordinary soldiers

explanation.surface: Troops stationed in a foreign country enjoy a fine vista.
explanation.definitionFit: A panorama is a wide, unbroken view of a whole area.

clue.text: Inventor sounding like a very attractive person

indicators.note: sounding like asks for a word pronounced the same as the phrase that follows

parts.note: a belle is a beautiful woman, the beauty of the ball

explanation.surface: An inventor whose name evokes good looks.
explanation.definitionFit: Alexander Graham Bell, credited with inventing the telephone, is a famous inventor.

clue.text: Son must have bravery, not wanting a whip

indicators.note: not wanting the letter means it is dropped from the word for bravery

parts.note: courage is another word for bravery

explanation.surface: A boy needs courage but would rather avoid being lashed.
explanation.definitionFit: A scourge is a whip used for punishment, historically for flogging.

clue.text: Locum educationist will provide rescheduled lectures — happy?

indicators.note: lectures that are rescheduled are rearranged, so the letters of the two words are reordered

explanation.surface: A stand-in teacher is pleased to take over rearranged lectures.
explanation.walkthrough: 'happy' looks like a question about mood, but it joins 'lectures' as the anagram fodder; 'will provide' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A supply teacher is a temporary teacher covering for an absent one, a locum in education.

clue.text: A he-man wandering around one Californian city

indicators.note: the scrambled letters go around the numeral, a container signal
wandering suggests these letters roaming into a new order

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A muscleman roams about a Californian city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wandering' rearranges A HE-MAN into ANAHEM, and 'around' puts that round I.
explanation.definitionFit: Anaheim is a city in southern California, home of Disneyland.

clue.text: Dilapidated Dorset home Pam totally transformed

indicators.note: a dilapidated building is falling apart, so these letters are broken up and rebuilt

explanation.surface: Pam's run-down house in Dorset has been completely made over.
explanation.definitionFit: Metamorphosed means changed completely in form, as a caterpillar into a butterfly.

clue.text: Communicate basic instruction for voter

definitions.meaning: to put something across is to convey or communicate it clearly
a voter is told to mark the ballot with an X beside the choice

explanation.definitionFit: Putting an idea across means getting it understood; read literally, it is marking a ballot with an X.

clue.text: Little bird to 'oller — and in French!

parts.note: to holler is to howl; with the dropped h of the clue's spelling it becomes owl without its first letter
et is the French word for and

explanation.surface: A Cockney yell, with a French conjunction thrown in.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe in 'oller shows a dropped H, so HOWL loses its H too.
explanation.definitionFit: An owlet is a young or small owl, so a little bird.

clue.text: This competitor getting nearer? Not first!

indicators.note: not first tells us to remove the opening letter of the word for nearer

parts.note: closer means getting nearer

explanation.surface: A runner closing the gap is told it will not be first place.
explanation.definitionFit: A loser is a competitor who does not win, the one who is not first.

clue.text: Form of belief that accepts terrible fate

definitions.text: Form of belief that accepts terrible fate

indicators.note: accepting something takes it in, so one piece holds the other inside

parts.note: deism is belief in a creator who does not intervene

indicators.note: terrible signals the letters of the next word are mangled

explanation.surface: A philosophy that resigns itself to dreadful destiny.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue doubles as the definition: a belief system that resigns itself to bad outcomes; 'terrible' and 'that accepts' do the work inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Defeatism is the attitude of expecting and accepting defeat, a belief that yields to fate.

clue.text: Quiet types at home, not drinking, cuddling dog, beginning to snooze

parts.note: in means at home, as in staying in

indicators.note: the abstainer letters wrap round the dog like arms in a cuddle

parts.note: TT, teetotal, means not drinking alcohol
Rover is a traditional name for a dog

indicators.note: beginning to asks for the opening letter of the next word

explanation.surface: Shy people stay in, sober, hugging the dog as they doze off.
explanation.definitionFit: Introverts are reserved, inward-looking people, quiet types by temperament.

clue.text: The control in that place

parts.note: a rein is a strap used to control a horse, hence control

explanation.surface: A remark on the controls found somewhere.
explanation.definitionFit: Therein is a formal adverb meaning in that place or thing.

clue.text: Turn away east abandoning a whole lot of mountains

indicators.note: the compass word abandons the letter, so that letter is removed

parts.note: taken as written before the letter is dropped
a range is a long line of mountains

explanation.surface: Someone heads off east, leaving a mountain chain behind.
explanation.definitionFit: To estrange is to alienate, to turn someone away from former affection.

clue.text: Old record is quiet when set alongside most recent

parts.note: P, piano, is the musical direction for quiet
the latter is the later or more recent of two

explanation.surface: A vintage disc set beside a newer one sounds soft.
explanation.definitionFit: Platter is dated slang for a gramophone record.

clue.text: The old man's weapon is something guard may want

parts.note: pa is a word for father, the old man, so his is pa's
a sword is a bladed weapon

explanation.surface: Dad's blade is what a sentry might ask for.
explanation.definitionFit: A sentry challenges anyone approaching and wants to hear the agreed password before letting them pass.

clue.text: Assailant's got nasty dogs

indicators.note: nasty suggests these letters turned into something rough and rearranged

parts.note: the possessive adds no letter; the word is used as written

explanation.surface: An attacker's dogs have turned vicious.
explanation.definitionFit: Alsatians are German shepherd dogs, the British name for the breed.

clue.text: Alter advertisement completely

parts.note: just can mean completely, as in just right

explanation.surface: A request to change a commercial entirely.
explanation.definitionFit: To adjust is to alter something slightly to make it fit.

clue.text: Inertia in hospital after a particular period

indicators.note: the hospital letter comes after the period, placed at the end

parts.note: a slot is an allotted period of time

explanation.surface: Lethargy sets in on a ward following a scheduled session.
explanation.definitionFit: Sloth is laziness, a reluctance to act, which is inertia.

clue.text: Ruler in the last month in hospital

indicators.note: the second in places last month's abbreviation inside the hospital word

parts.note: san is short for sanatorium, a hospital
ult, ultimo, is the old letter-writing abbreviation for last month

explanation.surface: A monarch spent the past month in a clinic.
explanation.definitionFit: A sultan is the sovereign ruler of a Muslim state.

clue.text: Board game hard for woman to follow

indicators.note: the woman's name follows the letter for hard, coming after it

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils
Alma is a woman's name

explanation.surface: A tough game, with a lady taking the next turn.
explanation.definitionFit: Halma is a board game in which pieces jump across a squared board.

clue.text: Liking nothing in sport

definitions.meaning: a fondness or strong affection for something
the term for a score of zero in tennis

explanation.definitionFit: Love means affection or fondness, and in tennis scoring it means zero.

clue.text: Shopkeepers deftly absorbing taunts? Quite the opposite

indicators.note: absorbing means one word takes in the other
this reverses the stated relation, so the taunts take in the skilful word instead

parts.note: jeers are taunts
well means deftly or skilfully

explanation.surface: Traders skilfully soak up mockery, or perhaps the reverse.
explanation.walkthrough: Read straight, WELL would absorb JEERS; 'Quite the opposite' flips it, so JEERS holds WELL.
explanation.definitionFit: Jewellers are shopkeepers who sell rings, watches and other jewellery.

clue.text: Ruins silver in wild parties

indicators.note: the silver symbol is placed inside the word for wild parties

parts.note: raves are wild, large-scale dance parties
Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

explanation.surface: The silverware gets wrecked at riotous parties.
explanation.definitionFit: Ravages, as a verb, means devastates or ruins.

clue.text: Like salad? No — it's criticised

definitions.meaning: salad is served raw, so the question denies it being cooked in an oven

explanation.definitionFit: Roasted means cooked in an oven, unlike raw salad, and informally means severely criticised.
